Choosing reference photos for an AI pet portrait: a practical checklist
Pettenderly

刚刚

编辑

A good reference photo starts with a familiar face. Before making a portrait of your cat or dog, set aside a few photos that show the details you would want to recognize in the finished image.

Start with one pet

Choose photos of the same cat or dog. Avoid mixing different pets into one reference set. Pettenderly accepts one to five reference photos for a pet portrait, so a small, consistent selection is a useful starting point.

Make the face easy to see

Look for a clear view of the eyes, ears and muzzle. If a favorite photo has deep shadows or the face is hidden behind a toy, compare it with a clearer photo before uploading. Check whether the coat markings you care about are visible.

Choose a look after choosing the references

A watercolor portrait, a royal costume and a sunny window-seat scene tell different stories. Choose the setting that suits the keepsake you want, while keeping your reference photos focused on the pet.

Review the result carefully

AI portraits can change facial details, coat markings and other fine features. Compare the finished image with your references before downloading or sharing it. Treat generated art as an interpretation rather than a promise of exact likeness.

About Pettenderly

Pettenderly is an online AI portrait studio for cat and dog owners. It creates downloadable digital portraits from your pet photos. Each successful image uses one credit; failed generations do not use credits. Credit packs and Pro subscriptions are paid products. Human-and-pet portraits and photo cleanup are beta features. Physical printing and delivery are not included.

Visit the official studio and check current plans: https://pettenderly.com/

This is a free guide published by the Pettenderly brand.
